# ADR-0018: Recovery classification for --resume

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-08-04

**References:** [ADR-0003](../adr/ADR-0003.md), [ADR-0004](../adr/ADR-0004.md), [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md)

## Context

Resume was a pure counter fold that discarded all information about how the run died. A shutdown line's absence (pod died mid-run) was never read. Dangling agent_start/done brackets were invisible. A pod that died while parked lost the approval entirely.

## Decision

One streaming pass over the log produces both resume counters (ResumeFold) and a typed Classification of the tail. plan_recovery maps classification to RecoveryPlan (NoOp/Refuse/Continue). Classification is derived from the log tail, never markers. New wire events (approval_wait/approval_resolved) bracket every approval. Policy: finished/solved is a clean no-op; escalated refuses to resume; budget honors a raised cap.

## Consequences

Old logs lacking the approval bracket degrade to died_between_iterations (preserving old behavior). Unknown shutdown.outcome or approval_wait.mode tokens degrade rather than error. The classifier encodes the emission grammar; tests live next to the scanner. Cost: new wire events must be emitted at every approval boundary.

## Alternatives Considered

### Streaming classifier over log tail with typed RecoveryPlan (accepted)


### Marker-based recovery: write explicit resume markers at crash sites (rejected)

- **Rejected because:** Markers are written before the crash, so a crash that prevents the marker write is invisible. Log-tail classification reads the emission grammar and degrades gracefully for old logs.
